newsitem.title: CUBA: No survivors found yet from Cuban air crash.
newsitem.headline: No survivors found yet from Cuban air crash.

text.p: Cuban civil aviation sources said on Saturday rescue workers had not yet found any survivors from the crash of a Cuban plane carrying 44 people that plunged into the sea late on Friday near the eastern city of Santiago de Cuba.
The sources, speaking about six hours after the crash, said coast guard vessels and air force planes were continuing to search for survivors.
The Cubana de Aviacion An-24 plane crashed into the sea minutes after take-off from Santiago on domestic flight number 787 to Havana.
The civil aviation sources gave no indication of whether any bodies or plane debris had been found during the search at the crash site near the mouth of the Bay of Santiago.
A civil aviation institute statement said there were 39 passengers on board, eight of them foreign, and five crew members. It did not give the nationalities of the foreign passengers.

The statement, read over a state radio news program early on Saturday, said flight 787 crashed into the sea minutes after take-off from Santiago at 9.55 p.m. EDT on Friday (0155 a.m. GMT Saturday). It made no mention of either survivors or deaths in the crash.

The statement said coast guard vessels and air force planes went to the scene immediately after the crash. It added the civil aviation institute had set up a state commission to investigate causes of the accident.
Cuba's worst airline disaster was in September 1989, when 126 people were killed in a Cuban airlines crash near Havana.
